Working in /opt/nxeon-v2 (Next.js app, branch design/v2) — a from-scratch visual/UX redesign ("Nexion") of a hosting platform's customer dashboard. This is a READ-ONLY audit — do not edit or fix anything, only report findings with file:line evidence.

CONTEXT: The main dashboard (app/dashboard/page.tsx -> components/nx/DashboardView.tsx) is confirmed part of the Nexion redesign (uses the new light/dark theme system: html[data-theme="light"], components/nx/* styling conventions). But a quick check shows app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx (the individual VPS/game-server management page — one page handles both VPS and game servers, since a game server is just a Server row with game-specific fields) imports almost entirely OLD components: components/customer/Console.tsx, SnapshotControls.tsx, BackupControls.tsx, NetworkingControls.tsx, ResizePicker.tsx, MetricsPanel.tsx, DiskUsageChart.tsx, ServerAccess.tsx — with only components/nx/Provisioning.tsx being a new Nexion component. Similarly app/dashboard/games/page.tsx (the games LIST) imports old components/portal/PortalHero.tsx and components/customer/DeployButton.tsx.

Your job — answer these clearly, with evidence:

1. **Theme support**: Do the OLD components used on app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx (Console, SnapshotControls, BackupControls, NetworkingControls, ResizePicker, MetricsPanel, DiskUsageChart, ServerAccess, ReinstallOs, GameTierInfo, ChangeGameSubdomain, ProjectAssign, ResourceLimitAlert) respond AT ALL to `html[data-theme="light"]` — i.e., do they use the `--color-*` CSS custom properties / Tailwind classes that flip in light mode, or are they hardcoded dark-only (e.g. literal `bg-slate-900`, `bg-[#0a...]`, `text-white` used as a color choice rather than through the theme token system)? Pick 3-4 of these components and check directly. Conclusion needed: if a customer switches to light mode on this page, does it look broken/half-themed, or does it actually already work because these components happen to use theme-aware utility classes?

2. **`app/dashboard/servers/page.tsx`** (the servers LIST, not the detail page) — same question: old design or Nexion-redesigned? Compare its className patterns against components/nx/DashboardView.tsx's patterns (Nexion components tend to use custom classes like `.card`, `.btn-deploy`, `.nx-*`, gradient/glow utility classes — check app/globals.css for what's Nexion-specific vs generic Tailwind).

3. **`app/dashboard/games/page.tsx`** — same question.

4. **New pieces that DO look Nexion-specific on the server detail page**: `components/nx/Provisioning.tsx` — what does it do, is it fully wired to real provisioning state (check what data/props it reads — real Job/Server status, or something hardcoded)? Also check `components/customer/GameSubdomainControl.tsx` and `components/customer/gamepanel/GameTierInfo.tsx` — are these NEW components added during this redesign (check git log/blame or just judge by whether they reference Nexion design conventions), and if so, are they real/backend-wired the same way the audits of other new features have checked (real server actions, not stubs)?

5. **Bottom line judgment**: if a real customer navigates from the new Nexion main dashboard (light mode, say) into an individual server's management page, will there be a jarring, obviously-unfinished visual seam (half old-dark-theme, half new-light-theme UI in the same page), or does it hold together acceptably because the old components already use compatible styling? Be concrete and honest — this is exactly the kind of thing that would embarrass a "seamless" production launch if missed.

Keep total report under 700 words, structured with clear verdicts per question. Do not modify any files.

# Nxeon v2 — the "Nexion" design fork **This is not the production tree.** It is a full fork of the Nxeon platform with a from-scratch visual language called **Nexion** built over the real backend. The code is real, the database is real, the money paths are real code — but `NXEON_SANDBOX=1`, so no VM is ever provisioned and no card is ever charged. Read `docs/NEXION-V2.md` next. This file is the operating manual; that one is the direction and the history of what has been built. --- ## Where you are, and what that changes This tree runs on **node-2** (`nxeon-fsn1`, `178.63.94.114`), and the work is meant to happen there. Check which box you are on before anything else: ```bash hostname # nxeon-fsn1 = node-2. Anything else = the primary node. ``` **On node-2 (`nxeon-fsn1`) — the normal case.** Edit here and build here: ```bash npx tsc --noEmit # always, before a build ./rebuild.sh # stop, build, restart. ~125s. ``` **On the PRIMARY node.** Do not build. The primary is an 8-core box that also runs the customer game-server VMs (darkeden-guard-sg, projectzomboid, dst, terraria, valheim…) and sits at load ~11 before anyone types anything. A `next build` there competes with paying customers for CPU. Edit if you must, then: ```bash scripts/deploy-node2.sh # ships the commit, typechecks + builds ON node-2 ``` It refuses to run on a dirty tree (it ships commits, not a working directory) and refuses to reset over commits node-2 has and the primary doesn't. **One source of truth at a time.** The deploy script does `git reset --hard` on node-2. Once you are working on node-2, the primary's copy is stale — do not deploy from it again without reconciling, or you will silently discard node-2's commits. The script checks for this and stops; take the stop seriously. ## The tree | | | |---|---| | Path | `/opt/nxeon-v2` | | Branch | `design/v2` | | Service | `nxeon-v2-web` on port **3021** | | Public URL | https://v2.q4w8zt3ky6vn2sm.nxeon.cloud | | Database | `nxeon_v2` on localhost — **separate** from prod and from the primary's own copy | | Logins | `/root/nxeon-v2-credentials.txt` (admin + a design customer account) | | Build log | `/tmp/nxeon-v2-build.log` | `rebuild.sh` skips the marketing site by default (~137 of ~195 route files, and it dominates a build we run by hand after every change). `NX_FULL=1 ./rebuild.sh` builds everything — do that before any staging or prod pass. Schema changes: `npm run db:push`. There are no migration files. The primary node and node-2 have **separate** `nxeon_v2` databases, so a push on one does nothing to the other. ## Reaching node-1 (live production) from here node-2 has **root SSH to node-1**, granted by the owner on 2026-09-11, because three things a Nexion session needs live only there: the board concept attachments (~500 MB across ~99 cards — the design source of truth), the production database (for checking a claim against real data instead of sandbox seed data), and the real production tree to compare the fork against. Use `scripts/node1.sh` rather than raw ssh — quoting a psql call through two levels of ssh is where this reliably goes wrong: ```bash scripts/node1.sh cards "dashboard" # find concept cards by title scripts/node1.sh board # list that card's attachments scripts/node1.sh pull # copy them to /tmp/board/ scripts/node1.sh db "select …" # read-only query against PROD scripts/node1.sh sh '' # anything else ``` **That grant is wide, and node-1 runs every customer VM, the production database and the mail server. Treat it as read-only.** Never write to the prod DB (the `db` subcommand refuses obvious writes, which is a guard against a slip, not a security boundary), never edit `/opt/nxeon`, never build there, never restart a prod service. If you genuinely need to change something on node-1, **stop and ask the owner first.** ## Rules that are not negotiable 1. **Never fabricate.** No invented stats, ratings, reviews, player counts, ETAs or capabilities. If a number cannot be read from the database or from a real upstream, the field stays empty and the UI says why. This tree has already had hash-derived star ratings and fake customer reviews removed once — do not reintroduce that shape. When a source cannot answer, say so; never render a `0` that reads as a real measurement. 2. **Never run builds in `/opt/nxeon`.** That is live production; clobbering its `.next` has taken the admin panel down before. 3. **Never `pkill -f` by pattern on either box.** `pkill -f "next start"` restarted live production once. Kill by port PID or systemd unit. 4. **Never `git add -A` in a symlinked worktree** — it can replace prod's real `node_modules` with a self-referential symlink. 5. **Ask before touching credentials** on live customer infrastructure, and before spending on any paid third-party tool. 6. **Never send a support-ticket reply** without explicit sign-off. 7. **`/opt/nxeon-sandbox` belongs to a different session.** Leave it alone. 8. Read the PNG back and actually look at it — a sliced game wordmark, a clipped top bar and an empty Mods tab were all invisible in the code and obvious in a screenshot. ## Things that have already cost hours here - **Bash `cwd` does not persist between tool calls.** Always `cd /opt/nxeon-v2 && …`. - **`git commit -m` with backticks in the message breaks.** Write the message to a file and use `git commit -F`. - **`git bundle create f A..B` with two raw SHAs** makes a bundle with no refs, which git refuses as empty. It describes the PRIMARY node. To avoid a very expensive mistake: - **Do not** run `systemctl restart nxeon-web nxeon-worker` — that is production. This tree's unit is `nxeon-v2-web`. - **Do not** publish docs to `revsports.ca/docs` from here. - **Do not** run `scripts/promote-production.sh` or `scripts/deploy-staging.sh`. - There is no post-commit auto-push hook on node-2, and there should not be: `design/v2` is a design fork, not something to push to `origin` casually.

## Nexion Theme-Consistency Audit — `app/dashboard/servers/[id]`, `servers/`, `games/`

### 1. Do the OLD server-detail components respond to `data-theme="light"`?

**Yes — they already work.** Checked 8 of the listed components (`Console.tsx`, `SnapshotControls.tsx`, `BackupControls.tsx`, `NetworkingControls.tsx`, `ResizePicker.tsx`, `MetricsPanel.tsx`, `DiskUsageChart.tsx`, `ServerAccess.tsx`). None use literal dark hexes for surfaces/text; they use `text-slate-*`, `bg-navy-*`, `text-white`, and Tailwind opacity-modifier classes (`bg-white/[0.06]`, `border-white/10`, `text-white/70`).

This is deliberate, not incidental. `app/globals.css` (lines ~19-27, 222-233, 380-450) documents that the entire `--color-slate-*` and `--color-navy-*` ramps are **inverted** under `html[data-theme="light"]`, specifically so all ~4,700 pre-existing `text-slate-*`/`bg-navy-*` call sites across the app "resolve without any call site touched." A separate, explicit block of attribute-selector rules (`[class*="bg-white/"]`, `[class*="border-white/"]`, `[class*="text-white/"]`, lines 419-449) retargets exactly the opacity-modifier idiom these VPS components use, converting dark-card lighteners into `color-mix()`-based washes against `--fg` in light mode. The comment at line 380 names the VPS panel explicitly as one of the files this covers.

Two minor exceptions found, both benign:
- `Console.tsx:206` — `bg-[#05060f]` inside `nx-dark-island` (the terminal). Islands are intentionally excluded from theming (rail/topbar/terminal stay dark in both themes by design — `globals.css` "dark islands" section).
- `MetricsPanel.tsx:140,143` — literal `bg-[#22d3ee]`/`bg-[#8a70fb]` chart-legend dots, cosmetic, unaffected by mode.

**Conclusion: light mode does not break these components.** They already ride the same token system as the Nexion redesign.

### 2. `app/dashboard/servers/page.tsx`

Old-lineage page (imports `PortalHero`, `DeployButton`, `ServersList` — all pre-`design/v2`), but all three consume the shared token classes: `.card`, `.btn-deploy` (globals.css), `text-slate-*`, `bg-white/[0.03]`, `border-brand-400/60`. `DeployButton.tsx` explicitly documents `.btn-deploy` as the shared CTA used "on every portal service page." Not visually Nexion-original, but not theme-broken either.

### 3. `app/dashboard/games/page.tsx`

Same pattern: `PortalHero` + `DeployButton` (old) plus locally written markup using `.card card-hover`, `text-slate-100/500`, `bg-navy-900/80`, `border-white/[0.06]`. All token-driven, all covered by the light-mode remap.

### 4. New pieces on the detail page

- **`components/nx/Provisioning.tsx`** — genuinely new (`git log` first appears at `a0a50f6`, a `design(v2):` commit) and genuinely wired: it reads `liveStep` sourced from `lib/provisioning-step.ts`, which parses the real worker's `Server.provisioningStep` field (documented checkpoints at `worker/index.ts:590-1010`). `simulate` mode (a timer-driven fake progress bar) is explicitly gated to `NXEON_SANDBOX` only and only when there's no real signal — production always renders from real worker state. Not a stub.
- **`components/customer/GameSubdomainControl.tsx`** and **`components/customer/gamepanel/GameTierInfo.tsx`** — **NOT new**. `git log --diff-filter=A` shows they date to commits `8038e81` and `e32ad4d`, both well before the first `design(v2):` commit. `ChangeGameSubdomain` calls the real server action `changeGameSubdomain` (`lib/actions-server.ts:349`). `GameTierInfo` is a real read-only informational card backed by real plan data, deliberately non-actionable per its own code comment (game plans are fixed bundles, can't self-resize). Both already use `.card`/`.input`/`.btn-secondary`/token colors, so they theme correctly too.

### 5. Bottom line

**No jarring seam.** The premise that these are "half old-dark-theme, half new-light-theme" doesn't hold up under inspection: the Nexion team clearly re-engineered `globals.css` as an app-wide token remap (slate/navy ramp inversion + attribute-selector rules for opacity-modifier white/dark idioms) specifically so ~18 legacy files, explicitly including the VPS/game panel, would theme correctly without per-component rewrites. A customer switching to light mode and drilling into a server's management page will see consistent surfaces, text, and cards throughout — the only intentional dark holdout is the terminal (`Console.tsx`), which is a deliberate "dark island" pattern also used for the nav rail, not a bug. This part of the redesign is visually coherent; it would not embarrass a launch.
